html:
The Battle of Dogali was fought on 26 January 1887 near Massawa, where an Ethiopian army under Ras Alula destroyed an Italian column of about 500 men marching to relieve a besieged fort.

Italy had occupied Massawa in 1885 and was pushing inland. Ras Alula, the governor of the north for Emperor Yohannes IV, attacked the Italian post at Saati and then caught the relief force in the open.

News of the defeat shocked Italy and led to calls for revenge. Italy pressed on, founded the colony of Eritrea in 1890, and was defeated again, on a far larger scale, by Menelik II at the Battle of Adwa in 1896.
sum: The Battle of Dogali was fought on 26 January 1887 near Massawa, where an Ethiopian army under Ras Alula destroyed an Italian column of about 500 men marching to relieve a besieged fort.
